attack_mechanism: For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.pc_nxt` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.pc_nxt` can alter the CSR write, trap/debug return, or stored `mstatus_mpp` value used by that MPRV branch; the state and data choices on this path depend on `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.alu_opa_mux`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.alu_sub`, `neorv32_cpu_control.branch_taken`, `neorv32_cpu_control.exc_buf`, and the remaining path guards. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation. The causal signal chain is `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.pc_nxt -> neorv32_cpu_control.exec_nxt.pc -> neorv32_cpu_control.instr_ma -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`.

The assignment `lsu_priv <= mstatus_mpp when mstatus_mprv = '1' else prv_level` makes `mstatus_mprv` the privilege-source selector. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.pc_nxt` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.pc_nxt` reaches that selector or one of its CSR update controls; the state and data choices on this path depend on `neorv32_cpu_control.ecause`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_we`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_re`, `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.
